newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Slain drug lord appanent victim of mob rivalry.
newsitem.headline: Slain drug lord appanent victim of mob rivalry.

text.p: A reputed drug lord gunned down in a luxury Bogota shopping mall was the apparent victim of rivalry between two drug gangs, judicial officials said on Thursday.
"It all seems to point to a settling of accounts between the Cali cartel and the Norte del Valle cartel," an official in the office of chief prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso said.

National Police sources said they too suspected that Wednesday's killing of Efrain Hernandez appeared to stem from infighting among drug gangs. But they said that it was too soon to say who was behind the crime.

The Noticiero Nacional television news programme said a lone gunman burst into an office in the Santa Barbara shopping mall where Hernandez was holding talks with a Lebanese businessman, identified as Alfredo Haddad Salvan, and shot both dead.
The TV report said its account was based on testimony from Herman Wexler, a German-born businessman who was wounded in the shooting but recovering at a Bogota hospital.
El Tiempo, Colombia's leading daily, said Hernandez and Haddad were killed by several gunmen, all apparently professional hit men.

Hernandez, a former policeman, had amassed a vast real estate empire since 1990 and was being investigated for suspected links to the Norte del Valle cartel. His former wife, a prominent Colombian model, was arrested on drug trafficking charges in Paris in September.
